design: randomized, blocked, paired crossover at task-template level

LOW.label: lower implementation capacity
LOW.implementation_resources: one qualified human implementer; ordinary editor, search, and deterministic tools; no generative code tool

HIGH.label: abundant AI implementation capacity
HIGH.implementation_resources: same qualification pool plus a frozen AI coding agent/model/configuration; up to four isolated candidate workspaces; human may prompt, select, and integrate

abundance_definition: HIGH is implementation abundance by assigned capacity: generative implementation is available and candidate capacity is doubled (4 versus 2) within the identical 120-minute implementation cap. It is empirically realized only if preregistered manipulation checks pass.
manipulation_checks: HIGH produces >=2 runnable bound candidates for >=70% of eligible task executions
median time to first runnable candidate in HIGH is <=70% of LOW
AI/model/configuration and candidate caps remain identical across all HIGH executions
controls: same frozen task contract, starting commit, context packet, gates, environment image, total stage definitions and repair cap
non-implementation AI assistance prohibited in both conditions
condition order randomized within repository/task/difficulty blocks; starting states reset; operators do not see paired outcome
gate order fixed: focused, repository/system, structural if applicable, governance boundary if applicable
estimand: paired HIGH-minus-LOW change in all-gates-valid throughput and in stage-specific binding status
anti_success_bias: Tasks are selected and difficulty-banded before assignment; HIGH is not tuned to observed failures and difficult implementation tasks remain eligible.
